newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to sell new TV rights for $95 mln.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to sell new TV rights for $95 mln.

text.p: The government said Tuesday that anyone interested in operating one of two new private television channels, which should come on line sometime next year, will have to pay $95 million in broadcasting rights.
Monica de Greiff, president of the National Television Commission, announced the steep fee in testimony to a Senate regulatory committee.

Industry sources had previously estimated the broadcasting rights would be sold for about half of the $95 million. But De Greiff said it was a "fair price" to operate one of the two available frequencies with national coverage.
She said "market penetration" was one of the main things the commission had looked at before setting the fee.
Bidding for the two new stations will open on Jan. 1 of next year and remain open until Feb. 24, De Greiff said.
Colombia currently has three television stations, one of which is non-commercial and state-run.

Likely bidders for the new stations include the Julio Mario Santo Domingo conglomerate, owner of brewing giant Bavaria and an industrial group headed by Carlos Ardila, owner of the Postobon soft drink and beverage empire.
In addition to the $95 million in broadcasting rights, industry sources said the cost of setting up and operating a new television station in Colombia would come to about $100 million.
